capabilities: Archive files to S3, Nextcloud or WebDAV storage, leaving a .remote marker
Rewrite internal links and frontmatter between [[file]] and [[file.remote]]
Stream remote audio, video and images in a built-in .remote viewer
Restore files from remote storage with SHA-256 and size verification
Delete remote objects via a context menu with confirmation modal
disambiguation: Not a backup plugin; it offloads large files to cloud storage to free disk space, and restoring deletes the remote copy.
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. Credentials are stored locally in data.json and never written to .remote marker files. Interface is bilingual (English and Russian). Exposes a public plugin API for other plugins and Dataview scripts.
intentEvidence: Important: This is not a backup plugin. It is designed to free up local disk space
motivation: The author built it to free up local disk space by moving large files out of the vault while keeping them seamlessly accessible inside it.
problem: Large media files (videos, audio, images, PDFs) fill up local disk space, and Obsidian has no built-in way to offload them while keeping them accessible.

relations.evidence: S3-compatible: AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO, Wasabi, Ceph
relations.plugin: S3-compatible storage (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, Wasabi)

relations.evidence: Nextcloud: Native Nextcloud WebDAV API with OCS public share link generation
Generic WebDAV: Standard WebDAV servers with optional read-only public CDN base URL

requires.name: S3-compatible, Nextcloud or WebDAV storage account

summary: Moves large vault files to S3, Nextcloud or WebDAV storage, leaving .remote JSON markers and streaming content on demand.
